title: The legacy template and catalog load path is replaced by the TSD admin template operations
source: RWB-E1-046 sections 4, 12 and 16; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17
description: RWB-E1-046 loads the merge field catalog and the template versions through the P4 reference-load path POST /admin/reference-loads with multipart file, table and validFrom, and refuses a repeat on the SHA-256 hash of the file. The TSD P6 v2 names instead five admin operations on the service itself - API-P6-003 GET /admin/templates to API-P6-007 POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/withdraw - and no reference-load path at all, and the TSD outranks the story for the module API. The mapping between the legacy request and the upload plus approve operations is therefore not given, while TC-E1-046-09 keeps the legacy path in its Data column and MSG-P4-002 as its refusal.
evidence: RWB-E1-046 section 12: "POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads (exists, module P4)" with request "multipart/form-data: file, table (\"template\" or \"merge_field\"), validFrom"; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P6-003 to API-P6-007 on /admin/templates and no reference-load row.
proposed: Serve the catalog and the template loads on POST /admin/templates plus the approve and withdraw operations of /api/recovery/comms/v1, keep the legacy file-hash rule as the idempotency rule of the upload, and record in the rwb-comms API file and in the wave 1 harness which legacy request maps to which operation; TC-E1-046-09 then asserts the refusal on the operation the load maps to.

title: The data-dictionary read has no contract dependency in the plan
source: Ownership Map v1 (sys_fields, sys_objects and sys_field_version owner P1); TSD P1 data dictionary; plan split slices for RWB-P6-E1046-APP
description: The catalog check of BR4 needs the field registry, which the target gives to P1 rwb-source-data as sys_fields and serves on GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-dictionary/fields. The read is real for the app story, but the plan declares no C dependency on an rwb-source-data contract for RWB-P6-E1046-APP, so the story cannot name the contract it builds against, and its fake is derived from the published data-dictionary document instead.
evidence: Ownership Map v1: sys_fields owner P1, basis "TSD P1 v3 T3.1 (metadata registry of entities and fields); API Specification v3 /admin/data-dictionary/fields x_module P1"; the slice RWB-P6-E1046-APP carries C = RWB-P3-E1043-CON only.
proposed: Add the rwb-source-data data-dictionary contract story to the C list of RWB-P6-E1046-APP, or confirm that the published source-data admin surface covers /admin/data-dictionary/fields; until then build against that document as a fake with one hop and a 2 s timeout (DP-11).

title: No source says where the template body object lives
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (body_ref) and T-A.2 (API-P6-005); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 17 and 41; Ownership Map v1 (document owner P5)
description: body_ref is typed ATTACHMENT varchar(400) in T3.1 and the content operation answers a binary, but no source says whether the reference names a P5 rwb-document object in the WORM Blob container or an object key of the service's own container. Architecture v5 gives P5 the metadata, custody, retention and the Blob files, while slide 17 gives P6 the proof of delivery and the templates; the story therefore stores an opaque reference and cannot fix the resolution rule.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1: "DF-REF-050 body_ref ATTACHMENT varchar(400) Yes"; Architecture v5 slide 16 rwb-document OUT: "FILE Azure Blob (WORM): files, 2.8 TB by 2031"; Ownership Map: document owner P5, template owner P6.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-046 (section 11 DF-REF-050, section 12 TemplateVersion bodyRef, section 17)
proposed: Treat body_ref as an opaque claim-check reference in this key, resolve it through the P5 rwb-document contract when the body is a document-hub object and through the service's own container otherwise, and fix one resolution rule in the rwb-comms API file before RWB-P6-E1052 generation is built.

title: The approver identity type of a template version is not settled
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (approved_by USER_REF uuid); RWB-E1-046 AC1, section 11 and section 12
description: T3.1 types approved_by as USER_REF uuid, while the legacy load files and every legacy acceptance criterion name the approver as the staff identifier "LEG-0001" and the approval is read from the file columns. No source says how the file value resolves to a uuid, whether the resolution happens at load time or at approval time, or whether the approval identity is a staff user or a service identity.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1: "DF-REF-063 approved_by USER_REF uuid No"; RWB-E1-046 AC1: "approved by user \"LEG-0001\" on 2026-11-10".
proposed: Keep "LEG-0001" in every fixture, resolve it to the USER_REF uuid at approval time through the directory the platform already uses for staff identifiers, and state the rule in the rwb-comms API file; if no resolution is allowed, widen approved_by to the staff identifier with the mapping documented.

title: The request and answer field names of the five admin operations are not in T-A.2
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.2 and T3.1; RWB-E1-046 section 12
description: T-A.2 names the resource of each answer (Template, TemplatePage, TemplateApproval, TemplateWithdrawal) and the multipart field names of the upload only. It gives no property list for the four resources, no page metadata, no withdrawal reason field, and no query parameter that selects the current version for a template code and language on a date, although the current-version rule and its three dates are what AC1, AC7 and AC8 and the wave 1 harness must assert.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 API-P6-003: "Response TemplatePage"; API-P6-006: "Request TemplateApproval"; API-P6-007: "Request TemplateWithdrawal", no property list in any row; TSD P6 T3.1 gives the template and merge_field field names only.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-046 (section 12 TemplateVersion property list, AC1 to AC8)
proposed: Baseline the four resources in RWB-P6-E1046-CON from the TSD P6 T3.1 field names in camelCase plus the platform page and error conventions, and add the current-version filter (code, language, on-date) to API-P6-003; the app story and the harness then build against the baseline.

title: The service-side guard on the admin operations is not specified and DP-08 is not declared
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 41 notes; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-08, DP-19)
description: The five admin operations declare a Documents area with rights R, C and A, and T6.2 says each endpoint declares its capability area and right, but no source says what the service itself checks when a request reaches it directly rather than through the edge. DP-08 with the rwb-access authorise contract is not among the patterns of this key, so no rwb-access dependency is declared, and the per-service login name the document's security scheme names is equally absent from the sources.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T6.2: "each endpoint declares its capability area and right"; Architecture v5 slide 20 (edge: gateway-bff) and slide 41 notes (REST under /api/recovery/<name>/v1 behind gateway-bff); the slice RWB-P6-E1046-APP carries no DP-08 and no rwb-access contract in C.
proposed: Enforce the declared area and right at gateway-bff for every admin route, and have the service refuse a request whose declared right is absent with 403 MSG-P4-002 from its own operation configuration; if a service-side authorise call is required, add DP-08 with RWB-P4-E1037-CON to this key in the plan.

title: The NSS and LINE OA request and result contract is not in the source set
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17; TSD P6 v2 T5.1; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 12
description: The ACE notification path is named only as 'REST ACE Common: notification path (SMS, LINE)' with INT-17 and INT-18 and the frequency 'As sent'. No request shape, no accepted-reference format, no result code and no callback path exists in the sources, and the legacy names the interface only through the Java signatures NotificationPort.send(NotificationRequest) and MessageResultListener.onResult(externalRef, channel, result, at).
evidence: Arch v5 slide 17 OUT: 'REST ACE Common: notification path (SMS, LINE)'; TSD P6 T5.1 rows INT-17 NSS and INT-18 LINE OA, approach 'ACE notification path', frequency 'As sent'; legacy section 12 published interfaces with no field list
proposed: The ACE notification path owner publishes its request and result contract with the NSS and LINE OA result-code maps before the wave 2 SIT entry; until then RWB-P6-E2022-APP and RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG use the stub of section 12.8 of the CON story.

title: The interaction ledger write and the contact-point failed count are not named in this key's contracts
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (interaction and contact_point_ext are P1); legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 11 and 12; metadata Contract dependencies RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P1-E1066-CON
description: The Ownership Map gives the interaction ledger and the contact point with its failed count to P1 rwb-source-data (DP-18, DP-05). The legacy expects InteractionLedgerApi.record, InteractionLedgerApi.updateDelivery and PartyApi.recordFailedContact, and the case timeline expects a message read that the module's API specification does not declare. The two contract dependencies of this key name neither the ledger operations nor the failed-count update, and RWB-P1-E1066-CON is the only P1 document in the dependency list.
evidence: Ownership Map: interaction owner P1, contact_point_ext owner P1; TSD P6 T-A.1 lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 with no message read; legacy section 12 'Owned elsewhere' block names InteractionLedgerApi.record/updateDelivery and recordFailedContact; metadata C = RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P1-E1066-CON
proposed: RWB-P1-E1066-CON names the contact-point read, the consent and verified fields, the failed-count update and the ledger record and delivery-update operations, or a P1 ledger contract is added to this key's Contract dependencies; until then rwb-comms calls the nearest named P1 operation and the gap stays open.

title: The retry mechanism and the five-attempt limit sit on two different readings of JOB-11
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-11); legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 4, 5 and 12; TSD P6 v2 T1
description: Architecture v5 slide 44 makes JOB-11 Outbox sender an every-minute outbox relay to Kafka owned by every service. The legacy makes JOB-11 a sender to the ACE notification path with a retry limit of 5 (DL11) and rule R-UNI-34 to the exception queue. The ACE notification path's own retry and dead-letter behaviour is documented nowhere, so it is not known whether an attempt is one relay window, one path call, or one of each counted together.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44: 'JOB-11 Outbox sender | every minute | every service | outbox relay to Kafka'; legacy section 12: 'Job JOB-11 Outbox sender: every minute; sends queued messages to the ACE notification path ... retry limit 5, assumed; DL11'; legacy section 5 X5: 'after the retry limit to the exception queue'
area: rwb-comms / platform relay / ACE notification path
proposed: The attempt counter and the exception rule R-UNI-34 are named as the message capability's own send attempt, counted once per relay window, and the path's internal retries are excluded from the count; the platform relay owner confirms the window semantics.

title: How the LINE OA read status reaches rwb-comms is not specified
source: legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 4, 12 and 13; TSD P6 v2 T5.1
description: The legacy requires a second status for the same send: LINE OA reports delivered and then read, and the interaction ends at delivery status READ. Nothing in the sources says whether that second status arrives as a callback from the ACE notification path into rwb-comms, as a poll of the path, or as a batch result, and the legacy interface names only MessageResultListener.onResult with no transport.
evidence: legacy section 4 step 7: 'the ACE notification path: returns the delivery result (NSS result code; LINE delivered and read)'; legacy section 13 configuration: 'LINE OA status map to DELIVERED, READ (data steward)'; no transport named in TSD P6 T5.1
proposed: The ACE notification path owner states the result transport for both channels; rwb-comms accepts either a callback or a poll as a result for a known external reference, and a result for an unknown reference is not applied.

title: The MessageRequest and Interaction field-level definitions are not specified
source: TSD P6 v2 Appendix T-A.2 API-P6-008; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 12
description: API-P6-008 names MessageRequest and Interaction and nothing more. The legacy names channel, templateCode, language and partyId on the request, and id, caseId, partyId, occurredAt, channel, direction, conductCheck, summary, sourceSystem, deliveryStatus and externalRef on the answer, with channel required, templateCode required, language defaulting to TH and partyId defaulting to the borrower. The types, lengths, formats and the optionality of the other properties are in no source.
evidence: TSD P6 T-A.2 API-P6-008 request 'MessageRequest', response 'Interaction'; legacy section 12 request and response rows; no schema fragment in TSD P6 T3.1 or the API specification
proposed: The names and the two closed value lists are fixed by RWB-P6-E2022-CON from the legacy and the TSD; lengths, formats and optionality are settled at the baseline review with the app and gateway-bff consumers.

title: The NSS and LINE OA egress credentials, certificate and endpoint are not specified
source: TSD P6 v2 T5.1 and T7 NFR-052; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 3 (DL30)
description: The deployment needs an outbound route to the ACE notification path with a client certificate, trust material and an endpoint, held in the platform secret store (NFR-052). The sources name none of them: no endpoint, no certificate issuer, no secret name, no egress timeout, and no network zone beyond the platform statement that the partner gateway sits in the DMZ. The legacy only states that the ACE notification path is available in the environment (DL30).
evidence: TSD P6 T5.1 rows INT-17/INT-18 with no endpoint; TSD P6 T7 NFR-052 'Secrets are held in the key store'; legacy section 3 precondition 'the ACE notification path to NSS and LINE OA is available in the environment (DL30)'
proposed: The ACE notification path owner and the platform security team publish the endpoint, the certificate issuer and the secret names; the chart carries references only and the egress check fails a release with a missing reference.

title: DP-08 is not in the pattern set and the case facts of the conduct check are not in the contract dependencies
source: metadata patterns applied (no DP08); TSD P6 v2 T6.1 and T6.2; API-P6-008 authorization 'Case record, right C'
description: The operation declares Case record right C with the scope applied, but DP-08 (the authorise contract and guard library of rwb-access) is not in this key's pattern set, so no rwb-access dependency is declared and no guard library is wired. The case facts the conduct check needs (the legal hold and the open deviation with the contact stop) are not in the Contract dependencies either: RWB-P3-E1043-CON is reference data only and the case read is P3's operation. TSD P6 T6.1 has no Case record area, so the letters for that area have no row of their own.
evidence: metadata patterns DP01, DP03, DP05, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP18, DP19 (no DP08); TSD P6 T6.1 columns 'Documents' and 'Litigation' only; API-P6-008 'Authorization: Case record, right C, scope applied'
proposed: The Case record right C is declared on the gateway-bff composite route to SCR-03 and the refusal messages MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are answered there; rwb-comms keeps a local guard that refuses closed when the case answer is missing, and the reconciliation of the T6.1 area is recorded.

title: The message delivery status vocabulary conflicts with LOV-DELIVERY
source: TSD P6 v2 T3.2 LOV-DELIVERY; legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 4, 9 and 13
description: The legacy sets the delivery status of a message to Sent, then Delivered, Read or Failed, and maps the NSS result code to SENT, DELIVERED and FAILED and the LINE OA status to DELIVERED and READ. TSD P6 T3.2 LOV-DELIVERY holds DELIVERED, REFUSED, UNDELIVERABLE and PENDING for the notice and WIN proof of delivery, so it carries neither SENT nor FAILED nor READ and it is the only list the module defines.
evidence: legacy section 9: 'Sets the delivery status on the ledger entry: Sent, then Delivered, Read or Failed'; TSD P6 T3.2 'LOV-DELIVERY | DELIVERED, REFUSED, UNDELIVERABLE, PENDING'; legacy section 13 result-code maps
proposed: The message status list is held as its own list in RWB-P6-E2022-CON (SENT, DELIVERED, FAILED, READ) and LOV-DELIVERY is left to the notice and proof-of-delivery capability; the data steward confirms or names the list.

title: The timeline shows the template of a message and the interaction ledger carries no template field
source: legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 11 and 15; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 customer_notice/template; Ownership Map interaction owner P1
description: SCR-04 Case timeline shows each message with its channel, template, conduct check and delivery status. In the target the message is not persisted in rwb_comms, the interaction is P1's and carries no template field (DF-INT-002 to DF-INT-029), and the notice table records notices only, so no stored row carries the template of a message.
evidence: legacy section 15: 'SCR-04 Case timeline ... shows each message with channel, template, conduct check and delivery status'; legacy section 11 interaction fields DF-INT-002 to DF-INT-029 with no template field; TSD P6 T3.1 notice and template only
proposed: P1 adds a template reference to the interaction record, or the timeline drops the template column; until then the timeline shows the channel, the conduct check and the delivery status only.

title: SCR-09 Exception queue has no owner in the sources
source: legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 5 and 15; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1; TSD P3 v3 queues
description: SCR-09 Exception queue lists the sends that failed after the retry limit. No source names the service that serves it: the API specification of rwb-comms declares no read for a message or for an exception list, and P3 owns queues and tasks without an operation for a send in an exception state. The outbox row in the exception state is the only record of such a send.
evidence: legacy section 15: 'SCR-09 Exception queue lists sends that failed after the retry limit'; TSD P6 T-A.1 has no such read; Ownership Map 'GET /queues' is P3's and carries no exception-send element
proposed: The exception queue is a P6 administrative read over the outbox rows in the exception state, or a P3 queue fed by a P6 event; the owner is declared before the screen is built.

title: The rwb-document contract used for the write-once generated PDF has no contract dependency row
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.2 and appendix T-A.2; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 (x-module P5, POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents); Ownership Map v1 api section; WP B-P6-01 story line of RWB-P6-E1052-APP
description: The story renders the notice to PDF and stores it through rwb-document as a generated, write-once document, and reads its document ID back. The module specification routes documents through P5 and the ownership map names the P5 operation, but no contract dependency (C) row for rwb-document is declared on the story, and no source read here fixes the request shape of that generated-document operation, its answer fields or its 2 s behaviour.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T5.2 (calls go through the published Java interfaces: P5 for documents); T-A.2 lists no document operation; Ownership Map api POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents owner P5; the story metadata C row names P3, P1 and P7 only
proposed: Add the rwb-document generated-document contract as a C dependency of this legacy key (or publish it in RWB-P5-E1052-CON) with its request, its answer and its failure shape, and record it on the service contract catalog

title: The field names behind the rwb-source-data data-product contract are not specified
source: TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (data-product contract); FSD P1 v3 A2.5 and the data-product reads; Ownership Map v1 api GET /data-products/{productCode}/records; legacy RWB-E1-052 section 11 (DF-ACE-*)
description: The customer name, the contact address and phone, the account balance with data_as_of, the freshness stamp and the proof-of-delivery facts are all read through the rwb-source-data contract, but no read fixes the field names that contract returns for DF-ACE-056 to DF-ACE-083, DF-ACE-001, DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-036 and DF-ACE-251 to DF-ACE-257, nor the exact record and page shape of the answer.
evidence: TSDs and the API specification name the operation and the data products, not the response field names; legacy RWB-E1-052 section 11 names the ACE view columns only
proposed: Publish the data-product record shape of DP01 Account and arrears and DP07 Legal in RWB-P1-E1015-CON, naming each returned field and its source column

title: Where the merge snapshot is persisted is not specified
source: legacy RWB-E1-052 sections 4 and 8 (BR12, the snapshot holds the code, column, business key and field ID); TSD P6 v2 T3.1 (notice, template, merge_field only); Template and Rules v1 DP-01
description: The legacy story requires a merge snapshot for every notice and forbids storing the merged value in it, but no table, document or store for the snapshot is named by the module specification, the data model extract or the architecture, and the notice table has no snapshot column. The decision record can hold a reference only if something holds the snapshot.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 lists notice, template, merge_field and signature_request and none carries a snapshot; legacy section 4 step 7 and BR12 require the artefact; no source read here names its table
proposed: Name the snapshot store in the rwb-comms physical schema (a snapshot table or a column on the local decision record) and publish it in the next physical-schema version

title: The request and answer field list of the notice operations is not specified
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.2 (API-P6-001 and API-P6-002 name NoticeRequest and Notice only); legacy RWB-E1-052 section 12 (NoticeResult record)
description: The endpoint detail names the request and answer types and the error statuses but gives no property list, no required flags and no example, and the legacy record gives six fields of a Java record. The response fields of the Notice answer, the request fields of NoticeRequest and the payload element list of NoticeGenerated beyond the legacy four are therefore settled by this run and not by a source.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 request NoticeRequest and response Notice with no schema; legacy section 12 NoticeResult(UUID noticeId, String state, UUID documentId, String holdReason, int templateVersion, List<String> messageCodes)
proposed: Publish the NoticeRequest and Notice schemas, with their required flags and the NoticeGenerated payload, as part of the rwb-comms API specification v5 and confirm them with the app stories of this key

title: The scope and right check of the notice operations has no rwb-access dependency row
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.2 (each endpoint declares its capability area and right; scope filters every query); Template and Rules v1 DP-08; WP B-P6-01 story line of RWB-P6-E1052-APP
description: Both notice operations declare the Litigation right and apply scope, and the legacy story refuses a role without the right with MSG-P4-002, but DP-08 is not among the patterns of this story and rwb-access is not in its contract dependencies, so no authorise call is built here. The source does not say what enforces the scope test on the notice read, and the person-not-on-case refusal of legacy AC8 needs the case party read rather than an access call.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T6.2 and T-A.1 access column; the story patterns list DP-01, DP-02, DP-03, DP-05, DP-07, DP-09, DP-11, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19 only; the C row names P3, P1 and P7
proposed: Record in the gateway-bff route and in the service contract catalog that the Litigation right and the scope test of the notice operations are enforced at the edge under RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and add DP-08 and RWB-P4-E1037-CON to this story only if the check moves into the service

title: Field DF-LEG-030 is party_id in the module specification and person_key in the legacy story
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-030 party_id CROSS_REF uuid); legacy RWB-E1-052 section 11 (DF-LEG-030 notice person_key) and section 12 (NoticeGenerationRequest.personKey)
section: Data; Contract 12.1 and 12.2; Business rules BR8 and BR9
description: The same field ID is defined twice with different meaning and type: the module specification gives DF-LEG-030 as party_id, a cross-reference to a party row, while the legacy story gives the same ID as notice.person_key and uses it as the idempotency key of a notice. The Workbench holds no party row under D-RCV-35, so a party reference and an ACE person key cannot be the same value.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 row DF-LEG-030 party_id CROSS_REF uuid; legacy RWB-E1-052 section 11 row DF-LEG-030 notice person_key; section 12 record NoticeGenerationRequest with personKey
proposed: Settle DF-LEG-030 with the data steward: keep person_key as the business key of the notice and give the party reference its own field ID, then correct either the module specification or the legacy field list

title: No operation in the ownership map raises a task on rwb-case
source: Ownership Map v1 api section (GET /me/tasks, PATCH /tasks/{taskId}); legacy RWB-E1-052 sections 4 and 5 (the task raise on a missing merge value and on a withdrawn template)
description: The story raises two tasks on the case — "Complete notice data" to the case owner and the withdrawn-template task to the litigation officer team — and the ownership map holds only the task read and the task update, no raise operation. The legacy story raises the task through an in-process CaseWorkflowApi.raiseTask call, so the target path has to be published by rwb-case before the app story can be built against it.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api lists GET /me/tasks and PATCH /tasks/{taskId} for P3 and no task-create path; legacy RWB-E1-052 section 12 lists CaseWorkflowApi.raiseTask(UUID caseId, String taskCode, String ownerRole, String reasonCode)
proposed: Publish the task-raise operation of rwb-case (or the event that creates a task) in RWB-P3-E1018-CON, and record it in the ownership map

title: The error code of each refusal condition on the notice POST is not fixed
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.2 (API-P6-001 errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503); FSD P6 v3 A2.1.4.3 and A2.3.4.3; legacy RWB-E1-052 sections 5 and 14
description: The operation lists 409 and 422 among its errors but no source says which condition answers which, the withdrawn template is a hold in the legacy criteria and a 409 refusal in the SMS criteria of the same module, and the repeat request is a replay of the first notice in one source and could read as a conflict in another. A consumer cannot write a reliable error assertion from the sources alone.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 lists the statuses only; FSD P6 v3 AC-EXC-P6-003-02 (template withdrawn answered 409 MSG-P6-003) against legacy RWB-E1-052 AC4 (notice held with hold_reason TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN); FSD AC-EXC-P6-001-04 (the same key replays 201)
proposed: Publish one error row per condition for API-P6-001 in the rwb-comms contract: the withdrawn-template hold answered with the notice in state Held, the repeat with a different key answered 409, and a missing field answered 422

title: The hold reason value set is not enumerated in a list of values
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2 (no LOV for hold_reason) and T3.1 (DF-LEG-032 hold_reason varchar(30)); legacy RWB-E1-052 AC3 and AC4
description: The notice carries a hold reason and two values appear in the legacy criteria, POSTAL_ADDRESS and TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, but no list of values holds the set, so a third hold reason can be introduced without a contract change and a consumer cannot enumerate the answer.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-LANG, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-SENT-TYPE, LOV-SIGN-METHOD, LOV-SIGN-STATUS and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS and no hold reason; legacy AC3 and AC4 name the two values in the criteria
proposed: Add a LOV-HOLD-REASON reference list carrying POSTAL_ADDRESS and TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN and any later value, and read it through the reference-data contract

title: The NoticeGenerated payload element list is not enumerated
source: legacy RWB-E1-052 section 12 (NoticeGenerated: noticeId, caseId, type, templateVersion); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data)
description: The legacy story fixes four payload elements and the architecture fixes the envelope and the no-personal-data rule, but no source gives the full element list of NoticeGenerated, so the template identifier and a generated timestamp are added by this run and every consumer of rwb-decision and the reporting read model builds against an unconfirmed schema.
evidence: legacy section 12 table row Event published NoticeGenerated (EV-13): noticeId, caseId, type, templateVersion; Architecture v5 slide 42 notes on the envelope and the key only
proposed: Publish the NoticeGenerated schema in the AsyncAPI document of rwb-comms, naming noticeId, caseId, templateId, templateVersion, noticeType and generatedAt, and confirm it with the consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting

title: The WIN dispatch file, its acknowledgement and the INT-15 proof result record have no layout and no owning operation in the sources
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 4 and 12 (INT-14 out, INT-15 back); TSD P6 v2 T5.1 and T3.1; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41
description: rwb-comms writes the approved notices of a business date to the WIN dispatch file (INT-14), reads back an acknowledgement that names the barcode and the sent date, and applies the proof results of INT-15 to the same barcode. The sources name the interfaces and the facts but give no file name, no record layout, no acknowledgement field list, no proof result record and no owning operation to call: TSD P6 v2 T5.1 lists INT-14 as "WIN, Out, File, Daily" only, and Architecture v5 gives the loop as an activity "deliverFile (WIN letters)" of rwb-integration without a payload. The legacy story also reads the proof rows from v_ace_pod inside the comms module, which the target forbids (DP-05), so the read path itself has to be decided.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T5.1: "INT-14 | WIN | Out | File | Daily"; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17: "TMP Document: generate letter, Decision: child: approval, Integration: deliverFile (WIN letters)"; legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12: "The INT-15 results are not a Workbench load: ACE ingests them, and DeliveryResultReader takes the Refused and Undeliverable results from v_ace_pod"; no column list or acknowledgement field appears in the legacy story, the FSD P6 A2.2 or the TSD P6 T-A.
proposed: Fix the file name, the record layout, the acknowledgement fields and the proof result record with the WIN owner and the rwb-integration owner in the baseline review of RWB-P6-E2021-CON, publish them there, and read the proof results through the rwb-integration contract (or add C RWB-P1-E1066-CON if the proof facts must come from rwb-source-data).

title: The daily reconciliation REC-05 that the legacy story names has no owner and no mechanism in the sources
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 13 (done when); Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-04 reconciliation, rwb-source-data); TSD P6 v2
description: The legacy story is done when "REC-05 shows no break for the synthetic month of notices", so the dispatch loop depends on a reconciliation of notices against the WIN file and the proof. No source names the owner of REC-05, its frequency, its break definition or its output: Architecture v5 gives reconciliation to rwb-source-data as JOB-04 on the ACE data ready event, the TSD P6 has no reconciliation section, and the FSD P6 does not mention REC-05. The app, contract and operations stories therefore cannot declare a reconciliation job, a series or a runbook entry for it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 13: "Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, and REC-05 shows no break for the synthetic month of notices"; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44: "JOB-04 | Reconciliation | Airflow: ACE data ready | rwb-source-data | event-triggered workflow"; no REC-05 row appears in TSD P6 v2, FSD P6 v3 or the Architecture v5 extract.
proposed: Assign REC-05 to the reconciliation story of rwb-source-data (JOB-04) and add the notice break count and its series there; until then the proof-window series and the unacknowledged-file alert are the evidence that stands in its place.

title: The arithmetic of the 7-day proof window on the sent date is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 AC6 and section 13; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 20 (proof window 7 days); TSD P6 v2 T3.2
description: R-LIT-08 and the legacy story fix the proof window as 7 days from sending, and AC6 shows a notice sent on 2026-12-15 becoming Unserved on the run of 2026-12-22 while a notice sent on 2026-12-16 stays Sent. The sources do not state whether the 7 days are calendar days or working days, whether the sent date counts, and whether a proof result that arrives on the seventh day and after the run is still inside the window. The window is set as data, but its arithmetic decides the boundary of a notice period that can be challenged.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-021 AC6: "notice N-0102 ... Sent with sent date 2026-12-15 ... When JOB-10 runs on 2026-12-22 ... Then notice N-0102 is Unserved with delivery status PENDING ... Then notice N-0103 stays Sent"; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 20: "Proof window 7 days"; no day-count rule appears in the FSD P6 or the TSD P6.
proposed: Confirm with the business lead and Legal counsel that the window is 7 calendar days counted from the sent date and that a notice is unserved on the first run on or after sent_date plus 7 days, then record the value and the rule in the reference data with its version.

title: The scope test of the notice read has no scope source in the dependencies of this story
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 AC11 (MSG-P4-003); Template and Rules DP-08 and the pattern list of this key; Ownership Map v1 (P4 authorise)
description: Legacy AC11 refuses a GET for a notice outside the caller's scope with status 404 and MSG-P4-003. The target enforces the capability area and the right through the authorise contract of rwb-access (DP-08) at gateway-bff, but DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this key and neither RWB-P4-E1037-CON nor any P4 story is a dependency of RWB-P6-E2021-APP. The scope itself (owner, queue, team, region) is case data of rwb-case, and no row of the contract dependencies names a read that returns it for this purpose.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-021 AC11: "Given notice N-0200 belongs to a case outside the scope of LIT-0101 ... Then the response is status 404 with MSG-P4-003"; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-08: "Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library, H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, C RWB-P4-E1037-CON", absent from the patterns of RWB-P6-E2021-APP; Ownership Map v1 api lists POST /authorise and GET /cases/{caseId} but no scope read for a notice.
proposed: Declare the capability area and the right per operation in RWB-P6-E2021-CON and let gateway-bff ask rwb-access (DP-08) before the call; serve the scope fact from the rwb-case case read that the contract already consumes, or add C RWB-P4-E1037-CON if rwb-comms must decide the scope inside the service.

title: The deployment slots, the worker placement and the alert thresholds of the dispatch loop are not stated
source: TSD P6 v2 Appendix T-B (DL35 deployment slots); Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-10 Airflow file window and workers); Template and Rules §R7.2 s17
description: RWB-P6-E2021-OPS deploys an api deployment and a worker deployment of rwb-comms, registers the 16:00 Schedule and wires six alerts. The sources give no deployment slot, no namespace beyond rwb-recovery, no replica count, no resource size and no alert threshold: the TSD P6 leaves DL35 "deployment slots" open, Architecture v5 says only that JOB-10 runs as an Airflow file window with the workers of rwb-comms and rwb-integration, and the legacy story gives no operational value beyond the 16:00 time and a 7-day window.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 Appendix T-B: "DL35 | Deployment slots | (open)"; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44: "JOB-10 | WIN notices | 16:00 | rwb-comms + integration | Airflow file window + workers" and "JOB-11 | Outbox sender | every minute | every service | outbox relay to Kafka"; no threshold, replica or slot value appears in FSD P6 v3, TSD P6 v2 or the legacy story.
proposed: Set the slot and the replica counts in the three values files once DL35 is decided, confirm the six alert thresholds at UAT and record the agreed values in the runbook entry each alert links.

title: The Notice response fields and types are named by the legacy story but not specified by the contract sources
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12 (POST and GET answers); TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 (API-P6-001 and API-P6-002 name the Notice schema only)
description: The legacy story lists the Notice answer as id, caseId, documentId, noticeType, sentDate, barcode, callbackDate, deliveryStatus and sentType, and the TSD P6 names the response as "Notice" without a field table. The dispatch fields holdReason, dispatchFileId and dispatchAttempts are table columns of TSD P6 T3.1 and are not stated as response fields. No source gives the type, the format or the optionality of any of them, so the OpenAPI shape of the answer is a baseline decision and not a copied value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12: "Response | 201 Notice: id, caseId, documentId, noticeType, sentDate, barcode, callbackDate, deliveryStatus, sentType"; TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 API-P6-001: "Response | Notice" with no field table; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 gives DF-LEG-032, DF-LEG-033 and DF-LEG-034 as notice columns only.
proposed: Fix the nine legacy fields plus holdReason, dispatchFileId and dispatchAttempts as the Notice component in RWB-P6-E2021-CON, all optional except id and caseId, and validate the additive rule against the RWB-P6-E1052-CON Notice.

title: The handoff from the Airflow WIN file window to the 16:00 Temporal Schedule has no mechanism in the sources
source: Architecture v5 slide 44 notes (Airflow opens the WIN file window, JOB-10); TSD P6 v2 T5.1 and Appendix T-B; DP-10
description: Architecture v5 replaces the Quartz job of the legacy story with a Temporal Schedule in rwb-comms and keeps the bank Airflow for the cross-system edges, where it "opens the WIN and debt-buyer file windows (JOB-10)". How the opened window reaches the Schedule is not stated: the sources give no signal, no HTTP trigger, no workflow start call and no ordering rule between the file drop and the run, so the operations story cannot test the handoff and the app story cannot fix the workflow's start contract.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 notes: "it opens the WIN and debt-buyer file windows (JOB-10)"; slide 44 row: "JOB-10 | WIN notices | 16:00 | rwb-comms + integration | Airflow file window + workers"; no handoff element appears in TSD P6 v2, FSD P6 v3 or the legacy story.
proposed: Agree the handoff with the Airflow owner and the platform workflow kit: the window signals the rwb-comms Schedule with the business date, the run records the date, and a rerun of the same date writes no second file; publish the row in RWB-P6-E2021-CON.

title: The message text of MSG-P6-005 and MSG-P3-005 is not given by the legacy story or the P6 extracts
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12 (errors of the POST) and section 14; FSD P6 v3 A2.1 and A2.2; TSD P6 v2 T-A.2
description: The POST answers 409 with MSG-P6-005 (the template of the notice is not approved) or MSG-P3-005 (a notice of this type is already in progress for the case). Both IDs appear in the legacy contract table, and neither text appears in the legacy story's message table, in the FSD P6 A2.1 and A2.2 validation tables or in the TSD P6, so the app and contract stories carry the placeholder rather than invent a wording.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12: "409 template not approved (MSG-P6-005) or a notice of this type already in progress (MSG-P3-005)"; the legacy section 14 table lists MSG-P6-008, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P3-004, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P6-004 only; FSD P6 v3 A2.1.3.1 lists VR-P6-001-1 with the MSG-P6-003 text only.
proposed: Take the two texts from the owning stories (the template approval of RWB-P6-E1052-CON and the case in-progress check of the case service) and copy them unchanged into this story's section 14 when they are published.

title: The pod and batch-status contract elements are not named in RWB-P1-E1066-CON
source: Ownership Map v1 (P1 rows); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 42; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (change note); legacy story RWB-E1-055 section 12
description: rwb-comms must read the proof-of-delivery rows of a business date and the completeness of the ACE batch of source WIN to set callback_date, delivery_status and state Delivered, and must read no row of a date whose batch is not COMPLETE. The target gives P6 no grant on recovery.v_ace_pod, v_ace_batch_status or v_ace_account and makes rwb-source-data the single reader through RWB-P1-E1066-CON. Neither the Ownership Map nor the architecture extract names the operation or the field of that contract for the pod records, the batch status, the feed version or the stale marker, so the consumed row, its fake and its assertions cannot be fixed from a source.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 notes, rwb-comms IN: "REST POST /notices (request); GET /cases/{id}/notices | events DeviationRaised / Cleared (contact stop); TreatmentApproved, PaymentMissed; CaseStateChanged | Temporal NoticeDispatchWorkflow" — no pod or batch read appears. FSD P6 v3 change note: "proof of delivery reads `v_ace_pod`". Ownership Map v1 tables give v_ace_* no P6 grant and no P1 api row for a pod read.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-055 (AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC10, AC11)
proposed: Add the pod records, freshness and batch-status elements of the pod data product to RWB-P1-E1066-CON, with the business date, the feed version, the batch status and the stale marker; until then consume them at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP07/records and GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness, one hop with a 2 s budget, as RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG already assumes.

title: No access guard story covers the notice read of rwb-comms
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T-A.2 (API-P6-002); Ownership Map v1 api rows for P4; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-08
description: The notice read declares the Litigation area and the R right from the TSD P6 T6.1 matrix, and TC-E1-055-12 asserts that a role without that right is refused with MSG-P4-002. DP-08 is not among the patterns applied to legacy RWB-E1-055, and neither the build dependencies nor the contract dependencies of the key name any rwb-access story, so the enforcement point of the declared right is gateway-bff for the screen path and the local guard of the operation itself has no owner, no contract and no test fixture of its own.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.2, API-P6-002: "Authorization | Litigation, right R, scope applied". Template and Rules v1 §R5.5: "DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON"; DP-08 is absent from the pattern list of RWB-E1-055 in the split plan. Ownership Map v1 lists POST /authorise and GET /me/permissions for P4 only.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-055 (TC-E1-055-12, legacy AC1 scenario on the notice read)
proposed: Record in the rwb-comms API document that the declared area and right are enforced at gateway-bff on the screen path, and either add the P4 authorise contract as a C dependency of RWB-P6-E1055-APP or state that a service identity call carries no user right; the guard library is a platform item and no guard is written in this story until that is settled.

title: The stored letter retrieval is not named in RWB-P5-E1054-CON
source: Ownership Map v1 tables (document, P5); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-11; legacy story RWB-E1-055 sections 4 and 12
description: The INT-14 record set carries a document reference for each notice, and the app story must know that the letter exists behind notice.document_id before the file is built. RWB-P5-E1054-CON is the C dependency of the key, but no source names the operation or the element of the document hub that returns the stored letter of a notice, nor whether it returns metadata or a claim-check handle, so the consumed row, the fake and the assertion on one letter per notice cannot be fixed from a source.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 notes, rwb-comms OUT: "Temporal Document: generate letter · Decision: child: approval · Integration: deliverFile (WIN letters)"; Ownership Map v1 tables: document owner P5; TSD P6 v2 T3.3: "notice | document_id | document | Many to 0 or 1"; no document operation is named in the legacy story or in the P6 appendix T-A.
proposed: Name the document read and the claim-check handle in RWB-P5-E1054-CON; until then consume GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} as the ITG harness already does, one hop with a 2 s budget, and treat a missing letter as a held notice rather than a dispatched one.

title: The INT-14 and INT-15 fixed layouts, their record keys and their transport are not in the source material
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.1 (INT-14); legacy story RWB-E1-055 sections 4, 12 and 16; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.2
description: The dispatch builds one INT-14 file with a record per notice and a trailer with the record count, and the proof read consumes the INT-15 fields barcode, sent date, callback date, delivery status and sent type. The source names the fields but not their order, length, delimiter, encoding, the record keys, the file naming, the header and trailer layout, the SFTP directory, the acknowledgment file layout or the trailer of INT-15. Those are the WIN owner's documents and they are not part of the material this run reads, so the file element of the contract baseline and the synthetic fixture files cannot be fixed from a source.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T5.1: "INT-14 | WIN | Out | File | Daily". Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 12: "Output | INT-14 file: ContractNO, addressee, address, notice type, template version, document reference; trailer with the record count"; section 4 step 4: "the sent date (DDMMYYYY), Barcode and Sent Type (s2t mapping of INT-14)" — no layout, no record key and no transport detail.
proposed: Attach the WIN owner INT-14 and INT-15 specifications to the contract baseline as annexes with a version label; declare the file element as a shape until then, derive the synthetic fixture from the annex, and treat a layout change as a new file version rather than an edit in place.

title: The owner of REC-05 and of the References exception list is not named
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-055 sections 4, 5 and 8 (REC-05, X3, BR5); Ownership Map v1 tables (reconciliation_result P1, notice P6, data_product P1)
description: The legacy story runs a daily reconciliation REC-05 that lists a notice sent with no barcode after three days, and holds an unknown proof-of-delivery row on an exception list with check References. In the target the reconciliation result and the data-quality exceptions are rwb-source-data's while the barcode and the sent date of the notice are rwb-comms's, and no source says which service runs REC-05, which one owns the References list, and which one a platform administrator reads on SCR-45. The split decides who builds the check, who is paged and which service's contract the harness asserts.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 4 step 9: "each day, compares notices sent to WIN with barcodes returned (REC-05)"; section 5 X3: "The row is held on the exception list"; section 5 X6: "REC-05 break listed for the platform administrator". Ownership Map v1: reconciliation_result owner P1, notice owner P6; no REC-05 row and no exception-list owner appears in the map.
proposed: Rule that rwb-comms computes the barcode break on its own notice rows and publishes it, and that rwb-source-data owns the References list and the data-quality read; until then the break is a row rwb-comms writes and the held row is read on the P1 data-quality operation, as RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG assumes.

title: The WIN host, port, zone, certificate owner, container names and file sizes are not in the source material
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 44; legacy story RWB-E1-055 sections 3 and 17; Template and Rules v1 §R9
description: The infrastructure slice must open an egress path to the WIN SFTP endpoint, hold a client certificate the WIN owner accepts, name the staging area and the delivered-file store, and size both from the file the loop produces. No source gives the host, the port, the network zone, the certificate subject or its owner, the container or bucket names, the retention period, the file size of an INT-14 batch, the object counts, the worker pool sizes or the scaler caps, so every one of those values is a placeholder and a reviewed value per environment.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44: "JOB-10 | WIN notices | 16:00 | rwb-comms + integration | Airflow file window + workers"; legacy RWB-E1-055 section 3: "The integration adapters (P2) send and receive WIN files on the SFTP path agreed with the WIN owner"; no host, port, zone, certificate or size appears in any source read for this run.
proposed: Record the host, port, zone, certificate subject and owner, container names, retention and sizes as reviewed values per environment in the provisioning artefacts of RWB-P6-E1055-INF, and confirm them with the WIN owner and Security before the SIT cutover.

title: The deployment slot and namespace of rwb-comms, and the exact form of the JOB-10 Airflow handoff, are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-B (DL35); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 notes
description: The deployment registers one dispatch Schedule at 16:00 and records the handoff with the bank Airflow file window, but the TSD leaves the deployment slots open as DL35 and no source gives the cluster or namespace the service is deployed into, the name of the Schedule, or the task, the DAG or the signal by which Airflow opens the WIN window and hands the business date to the workflow. The Schedule name, the slot and the handoff therefore cannot be fixed from a source, and the deployment check and the runbook entry currently name the mechanism only.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 appendix T-B: "DL35 | Deployment slots" with no value. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 notes: "the bank's Airflow (replacing Control-M; for discussion) owns only the cross-system edges: ... it opens the WIN and debt-buyer file windows (JOB-10)" — no task name, no DAG and no namespace.
proposed: Fix the deployment slot and namespace with the platform team under DL35, name the Schedule and record the Airflow window call (the task, the signal or the parameter that carries the business date) in the runbook, and assert both in the registration step of RWB-P6-E1055-OPS.

title: No source gives the alert thresholds, the reviewed time of the late WIN batch or the Schedule state per environment
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; legacy story RWB-E1-055 sections 8 and 16; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.2 VR-P6-002-1
description: The deployment alerts on a file that is not delivered, a pod batch that is not COMPLETE, a dispatch count of zero inside the window, the outbox lag and a stuck workflow, and it must also hold a reviewed time after which the batch of the day counts as late. No source gives a threshold, a window, a band, an evaluation interval or that time: the legacy story names a stale period of one business day and an attempt limit of three, and the FSD names the stale message, but neither gives an operational value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 8 BR7: "The notice data product is stale one business day after the WIN batch was due"; FSD P6 v3 A2.2 VR-P6-002-1: "Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (`v_ace_batch_status`)"; Architecture v5 slide 44: "JOB-21 Stuck workflow scan every 5 min, platform, visibility query + alert" — no file, batch or dispatch threshold appears.
proposed: Set the alert values and the reviewed time of the late batch in the rwb-comms values files, confirm them at UAT with the service owner and the platform observability owner, and record each agreed value in the runbook entry its alert links.

title: Only one hold reason is named for a notice
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.2 AC-EXC-P6-002-02; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-032)
description: The notice carries hold_reason, and the state model of the loop includes a Held state, but the sources name exactly one value, TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, on a template that is withdrawn after approval. The other reasons a notice may be held - a conduct block, a consent stop, a failed decision record, an address that cannot be composed - appear as refusal paths in the FSD and the legacy story without a value on hold_reason, so the list, its owner and its version cannot be fixed from a source and the state table of this story carries one named value only.
evidence: FSD P6 v3 A2.2 AC-EXC-P6-002-02: "notice \"N-0101\" is \"Held\" with hold reason \"TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN\""; TSD P6 v2 T3.1: "DF-LEG-032 | hold_reason | TEXT | varchar(30) | No | None | Workbench" — no LOV is named for the field.
proposed: Publish the hold reason list as a versioned reference list with TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN as its first row, and add its other values with the business owner before the Epic 2 dispatch refinements land; until then a hold writes the one named value or a free-text reason from the holding rule.
